'''Johnnie James Morton Jr.''' (born October 7, 1971) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) during the 1990s and 2000s.  He played [[college football]] for the [[USC Trojans football|USC Trojans]], earning recognition as an [[1993 College Football All-America Team|All-American in 1993]].  Selected by the [[Detroit Lions]] in the first round in the [[1994 NFL draft]], he also played professionally for the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] and [[San Francisco 49ers]] of the NFL. Morton also had a brief career in mixed martial arts fighting in 2007.

'''Johnnie Harris''' (born August 21, 1972) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Mississippi State Bulldogs football|Mississippi State Bulldogs]]. Harris played in the NFL for the [[Oakland Raiders]] (1999–2001) and the [[New York Giants]] (2000–2003). He also
played in the [[Arena Football League]] (AFL) for the [[Tampa Bay Storm]] (1996–1998), [[Orlando Predators]] (2005), [[Grand Rapids Rampage]] (2006–2007), [[Philadelphia Soul]] (2007) and [[Dallas Desperados]] (2008). 

Harris also played two seasons in the [[Canadian Football League]] (1996–1997) winning a [[Grey Cup]] championship both times. He played one with the [[San Antonio Texans]] (1995) and two with the [[Toronto Argonauts]] (1996–1997).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://argoalumni.com/gill-hudspeth/|title=Gill-Hudspeth|website=Toronto Argonauts Alumni|date=January 17, 2016 |access-date=June 26, 2020}}</ref>

Harris was named the AFL Defensive Player of the Year and first-team All-Arena at [[defensive specialist]] in [[1998 All-Arena Team|1998]] after he set single-season league records in interceptions (11) and passes defended (33) while playing for the Tampa Bay Storm.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/news/os-xpm-2005-03-25-0503250250-story.html|title=Predators place premium on Harris|work=[[Orlando Sentinel]]|first=Vincent|last=Thomas|date=March 24, 2005|access-date=March 13, 2023}}</ref> The Storm's quarterback, [[Jay Gruden]], told his brother, Raiders head coach [[Jon Gruden]], to take a look at Harris, leading to his start in the NFL with the Raiders.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sfgate.com/sports/article/Raiders-Safety-Harris-Tries-to-Prove-He-Isn-t-Out-2915181.php|title=Raiders Safety Harris Tries to Prove He Isn't Out of His League|work=[[SFGate]]|first=David|last=Bush|date=August 13, 1999|access-date=March 13, 2023}}</ref>

'''John Eldon Zook'''  (September 24, 1947 – June 6, 2020) was an American professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] for 12 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played for the [[St. Louis Cardinals (NFL)|St. Louis Cardinals]] and the [[Atlanta Falcons]]. Zook played [[college football]] for the [[University of Kansas]].

Zook was born in [[Garden City, Kansas]], and grew up in [[Zook, Kansas|Zook]] and Larned.<ref>{{cite news |title=Longtime Atlanta Falcons DE John Zook dies at age 72 |url=https://apnews.com/e698419d11d709d5d22d7da690e76a37 |work=Associated Press |date=June 7, 2020}}</ref><ref name="hutch">{{cite web | title=The Hutchinson News Online Edition | website=hutchnews.com | date=2011-08-21 | url=http://www.hutchnews.com/Todaystop/Ghost-town-Zook-Kansas--1 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110821204037/http://www.hutchnews.com/Todaystop/Ghost-town-Zook-Kansas--1 | archive-date=2011-08-21 | url-status=dead | access-date=2020-08-25}}</ref> He was a three-year letterman, was picked twice for all-conference honors, anchoring one of the top defensive units ever taking the field at KU. He was an honorable mention All-American in 1967 and was a consensus [[1968 All-America college football team|All-America]] honors as the Jayhawks' defensive standout on the 1968 Orange Bowl-bound team, the year KU was named No. 6 by the [[Associated Press]]. Zook had 202 total tackles during his career, putting him at No. 4 on KU's all-time defensive line list. KU Coach [[Pepper Rodgers]] said Zook "never played but full speed from snap one to snap hundred. He was the most full-speed player on every snap that you could imagine."<ref>[http://www.kusports.com/football/all-american/ KU Sports.com] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090305020049/http://www.kusports.com/football/all-american/ |date=2009-03-05 }}</ref> He was also chosen in the KU All-Time team by the ''[[Lawrence Journal-World]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.kusports.com/football/all_time_best/ |title=KU Sports.com |access-date=2009-03-20 |archive-date=2009-02-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090207182845/http://www.kusports.com/football/all_time_best/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Zook was drafted by the [[Los Angeles Rams]] in the 4th round (99th overall) of the [[1969 NFL/AFL draft]]. He was traded to the Philadelphia Eagles and then by the Eagles to the Atlanta Falcons, where began his NFL career in 1969. Zook played 144 games in the NFL and was a Second-team [[1973 All-Pro Team|All-Pro]] selection in 1973. He had been a Second-team All-NFC selection in 1972 and 1973 and was voted to the 1973 Pro Bowl. Zook was traded to the St. Louis Cardinals in 1976 and finished his career there.<ref>[https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/Z/ZookJo00.htm Pro Football Reference.com]</ref>

Zook recorded the first ever safety for the Falcons franchise.

Zook died on June 6, 2020, in Kansas.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hummer |first1=Steve |title=Goodbye John Zook, a classic Falcon |url=https://www.ajc.com/blog/further-review/goodbye-john-zook-classic-falcon/9X9bDd5uUq3kBZY8jFJ4AO/ |work=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution |date=June 7, 2020 |language=english}}</ref>

As stated in the [[List of Chicago Bears seasons]], the Bears made it to the playoffs four of the seven seasons that Wojciechowski was a part of the team. In an article written and published by the ''Windy City Gridiron'', Wojciechowski was recognized as being one of the top undrafted free agents. He wasn't in their top-10 list, but was given and honorable mention at the end of the article.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dane |first=Noble |date=December 31, 2015 |title= Chicago Bears top-10 Undrafted Free Agents |url= https://www.windycitygridiron.com/2015/12/31/10693822/chicago-bears-top-10-undrafted-free-agents}}</ref>

Wojciechowski's first year playing with the Bears (1987) was legendary [[Walter Payton|Walter Payton's]] last year. (Payton's outstanding rushing and receiving season, just two years prior to Wojciechowski joining the team, was one of the reasons the Bears were fortunate enough to compete in and win [[Super Bowl XX]].)
